description: 15 CFR 734.20: releasing technology or source code subject to the EAR to a foreign national is deemed an export to that person's country, even entirely inside the US. Visual inspection or conversation can count.

aspect: Why Iran is different from other foreign nationals
description: ITAR prohibits licences for countries under US and UN arms embargoes. Iran is in that category, so licensing is effectively unavailable rather than merely slow. Iran-specific sanctions reach further still, covering technical assistance to Iranian nationals ordinarily resident in Iran even when temporarily elsewhere.
energy_note: Not a queue - a closed door.

aspect: The green card is the escape hatch
description: The deemed export rule applies only to foreign persons. US citizens, lawful permanent residents, and protected individuals including refugees and asylees are US persons and are NOT subject to deemed-export licensing.
energy_note: Genuinely good news, and widely misunderstood by employers.
notes: IMPORTANT for the narrative and for real life: status, not ethnicity, controls here. Employers who refuse Iranian-born green card holders on export grounds are wrong in law.

description: Licences take months, cost money and are rarely pursued for one hire when citizen candidates exist. The practical result is a blanket practice of not hiring non-US persons for controlled roles.
energy_note: No refusal is ever stated in these terms; the application just does not progress.

description: DOJ's position is that employers must consider all work-qualified applicants and obtain authorisation where needed. Blanket 'US citizens only' postings can violate the INA. The law is therefore on the applicant's side and almost never invoked.
energy_note: A remedy that exists but nobody uses.
source_name: Littler - discrimination and deemed export laws
notes: Layer-5 target: DOJ IER settlements involving citizenship-status discrimination in export-controlled roles.

description: BIS licence conditions for 3E001/3E002 permit most silicon technology (bipolar, Bi-MOS, Bi-CMOS, CMOS) but not compound semiconductors such as gallium arsenide or silicon-on-sapphire. The boundary is granular, so whether a given job is closed depends on the exact process node and material.
Defence, aerospace and national-lab work are among the better-paid engineering tracks. Exclusion is not a delay but a permanent narrowing of the career surface, compounding over decades.
money_note: Illustrative cumulative differential, NOT a measured figure.

aspect: Security clearance is a separate, also-closed track
description: Clearance adjudication is distinct from export licensing. Foreign preference and foreign influence guidelines weigh family remaining in Iran, so even a naturalised citizen faces a harder adjudication because of who his parents are.
notes: Adjudicative Guidelines B and C are public. Layer-5 target: DOHA appeal decisions involving Iranian family ties - these are published and searchable, and would be strong specific material.

description: In ISCR Case No. 05-12088 the DOHA Appeal Board REVERSED a favourable decision. The judge had credited that the applicant resisted Iranian pressure to give up her US citizenship, that her father had no regime ties, and that she was US-born. The Board held an applicant with close family in a hostile country bears a 'heavy burden', and that close cases 'should be resolved in the favor of national security, rather than in the favor of the Applicant.'
energy_note: Winning at hearing and losing on appeal for having relatives.
notes: Verify the case number against the full text before citing - DOHA URLs are by FileId, not case number.

description: ISCR Case No. 04-09473: clearance denied where the applicant's grandmother, aunt, uncle and cousins were citizens and residents of Iran, compounded by foreign passport use.

aspect: EXAMPLE - being persecuted counts against you
description: The pattern across decisions is that evidence the applicant's family had been TARGETED by the Iranian regime weighed AGAINST mitigation - because targeting establishes the regime's interest in them, and therefore the leverage.
notes: The single most counter-intuitive finding in the dataset, and strong material.

aspect: EXAMPLE - and it is not automatic
description: In one Guideline B/C appeal the Board expressly rejected the argument that denial is automatic, finding nothing suggesting a 'blanket' rule against applicants with close family in Iran - while still affirming the denial.
energy_note: Not a rule, just the outcome every time.

description: ISCR Case No. 07-00894 was GRANTED where the applicant had returned her passport to Iran, renounced Iranian citizenship, had no family, friends or financial interests in Iran, and all siblings and her mother lived in the US as citizens. The price of clearance was having nothing left in Iran at all.
energy_note: Clearance granted on proof of total severance.

aspect: EXAMPLE - the passport you cannot surrender
description: One denial turned on an applicant unwilling to surrender his Iranian passport because he needed it to settle his father's estate in Iran, while his eldest brother remained an Iranian citizen and resident.
energy_note: Choose: your father's estate, or your career.

aspect: SCENARIO - the role that quietly closed
description: Omid interviews well for a turbine aerodynamics role and is told the team is excited. Two weeks later HR emails that the position has been put on hold. It is reposted a month later, same wording, with 'must be a US person' added to the requirements. Nobody has done anything unlawful and nobody has explained anything.
energy_note: The door closes without anyone being seen to close it.

description: See EMP-004. DOJ's Immigrant and Employee Rights section has penalised Clifford Chance (USD 132,000), Honda Aircraft (USD 44,626 plus monitoring), American CyberSystems and General Motors for exactly the exclusions described here.
energy_note: It is not just unfair. It has been found unlawful, repeatedly.
